page: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads, running on an Intel Xeon 8175M processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Compute resources are coupled with 64.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per virtual core. The platform operates on the x86_64 architecture and supports instruction sets including AVX-512, AES, and FMA. This instance type includes no integrated local storage and no hardware GPUs, relying on networked block storage for non-volatile disks and providing a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations position the m5.4xlarge in the average performance tier across multi-threaded operations, contrasted by weaker single-core processing capabilities. While multi-core benchmarks such as PassMark CPU (14,441.4) and Geekbench multi-core (6,542.0) place within typical median distributions, single-threaded tests such as Geekbench single-core (1,034.0) and gzip compression (21.8 GB/s) register in the lower quartile. The memory subsystem delivers consistent throughput, measured at 87.77 GB/s for large uncached reads and 45.25 GB/s for large writes, enabling 13.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.92 GB/s in static web serving benchmarks.

The primary tradeoff of the instance lies in its architectural generation. While its dedicated multi-threaded compute and stable 5 Gbps baseline networking support consistent enterprise operations, its older Skylake-era cores offer lower single-thread efficiency compared to newer instance tiers. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the resource ratio delivers predictable throughput for memory-reliant, horizontally scaled workloads without the overhead of unneeded GPU hardware. Best-fit deployments include backend application servers, containerized microservice hosts, relational database engines using attached network volumes, and batch ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory across 8 physical Intel Xeon 8175M cores clocked at 3.1 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support, it features a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core, a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps, and no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates average multi-core and memory bandwidth performance alongside lower single-core execution speeds, generating 13.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.92 GB/s in static web serving. The balanced resource configuration makes this server suited for intermediate relational databases, distributed microservices, caching layers, and general enterprise application hosting.
